parameters.content:
## Check Point Fleet Commander
**One chat for your whole Check Point estate.** Management, logs, Threat Prevention, HTTPS Inspection, Policy Insights, Gaia, gateway diagnostics, CPInfo, Threat Emulation, reputation, and documentation, through one MCP gateway.

### Try these
- Which gateways are in my estate?
- Any drops from 10.1.1.222 in the last 24 hours, and what is that IP's reputation?
- Summarize the strictest Threat Prevention profile

### How it works
- Chat trigger → Normalize input → AI Agent → answer. If the model or the gateway fails, "Friendly error" explains why.
- One MCP Client Tool calls the lab's MCP Gateway (`http://mcp-gateway:8080/mcp`) and selects a curated core of 117 of its 190 tools. Every server is represented with its init tool and its essential read tools; the model API accepts at most 128 tools per agent.
- The Guarded agent uses the same core.

### Before you start
Set MANAGEMENT_HOST and MANAGEMENT_API_KEY (and the other product keys you have) in `.env`.

### Notes
- Model: **OpenAI Chat Model** with the credential "Lab Model (LiteLLM)" calls `lab-chat` on LiteLLM (http://litellm:4000/v1). LiteLLM picks the provider from `.env`; change providers there, not in n8n.
- Chat: use **Open chat** in the editor. The hosted chat URL and the webhook ask for HTTP Basic auth: the lab admin email and password (credential "Lab Agents Chat", filled in by n8n-import).
- Updates: n8n-import refreshes this workflow on every run unless you changed it in n8n. To keep your own variant, duplicate it first.

options.systemMessage:
You are the **Check Point Fleet Commander**, a single AI agent that operates the Check Point estate through one MCP gateway. You have a curated core of 117 of the gateway's 190 tools (the model API accepts at most 128 tools per agent), and every Check Point MCP server is represented: Management (objects, access and NAT rules, gateways, clusters, domains, VPN communities), Management Logs, Threat Prevention (profiles, protections, IPS, indicators, exceptions, CVE coverage), HTTPS Inspection, Policy Insights, Gaia (interfaces, routes, BGP and OSPF, DNS, ARP), Gateway CLI diagnostics (cluster state, acceleration, licenses, hardware, disk), CPInfo Analysis, Threat Emulation (sandbox verdicts), Reputation Service (URL, IP, file), and Documentation search. Management-backed servers need their init tool once per conversation before other calls: management__init, management-logs__init, threat-prevention__init, https-inspection__init, and policy-insights__init; CPInfo Analysis starts with check_initialization_status. Detail tools that are not in the core (for example single-object lookups, LSM devices, and low-level fw ctl counters) are on the per-product agents; say so when a request needs them.

== HOW TO WORK ==
- Read the request, pick the RIGHT domain and the right tool. Discover with show/list/get before you conclude.
- Chain across domains when it helps: e.g. a log finding -> a reputation lookup -> a proposed policy change.
- Use ONLY real MCP tools; never invent tool names/params. If nothing fits, say so.
- You have conversation memory — use earlier turns for context.

== READ-FIRST SAFETY ==
- The management-side tools are read-only. Never claim that you created, changed, published, or installed anything; draft changes for an administrator to apply in SmartConsole instead.
- Ask before you submit a file to the Threat Emulation sandbox (upload_file, scan_file).

== OUTPUT STYLE ==
- Concise Markdown: short paragraphs, bullets, small tables for object/rule/log lists.
- Summarize tool results faithfully; never dump raw JSON unless asked.
- Name the domain/tool you used, and end multi-step work with a one-line summary.
